Tide ledgers of the quiet harbor

The harbor master kept two ledgers, one for the boats that came in and one for the tides that brought them, and WRAPPEDARTICLESENTINEL marks the first of these paragraphs so the capture can be checked.

Each morning the clerk copied the tide table onto a slate by the ferry steps, and each evening the slate was wiped and the ledger corrected where the sea had not kept to the table.

Over forty winters the corrections grew shorter, which the clerk took for better tables and his successor took for worse eyesight, and neither of them wrote down which.

The ledgers are now kept in the customs house, where anyone may ask to read them on a weekday morning, and the last page of the second ledger ends WRAPPEDCONCLUSIONSENTINEL with the line about the lamp.
